requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req124-mobile-tenant-config.md per WF-02 Step 1b's standard procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md). Read the design artefact directly -- do not read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute. Give explicit attention to three open questions the design itself flags rather than silently resolving: OQ-1 (locales/default_locale/branding/environment_kind sourced from global config, not per-tenant, because Tenant schema has no backing column and no migration is authorized for this requirement -- confirm this is an acceptable scope boundary, not a silent under-delivery of MOB-2), OQ-2 (mobile route has no ?host= branch, only ?slug=), and OQ-3 (branding's internal sub-schema is the design's own proposal, not pinned by any existing contract). Also confirm the new-route-vs-discriminator decision in §1 is adequately justified (it is a real design choice with tradeoffs stated, not a placeholder) and that the exact-shape test strategy in §9 (Map.keys sorted-equality assertion) and the unknown-slug/anti-enumeration justification in §4 are both concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER and ELIXIR-DEV to build against without further judgement calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every MUST/acceptance criterion in the requirement has a corresponding design element -- no TBD/deferral language
Function signatures fully specified: name, inputs, outputs, error cases (including mobile_config_map/1's exact 5-key shape)
Error handling shape stated as tagged tuples / explicit branches, not left implicit
No implementation code present -- signatures and type shapes only, no .ex code bodies

result.summary: lib/letflow/design/req124-mobile-tenant-config.md read in full and cross-checked against lib/letflow/routers/tenant_config.ex, lib/letflow/router.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex, and docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2 directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's self-report). All 5 gate checks pass. Corrected premises (design §0) verified true: TenantConfig is not a stub (REQ-078 implemented it, forwarded outside ApiPipeline), and AuthPipeline's call/2 has no bypass branch -- confirmed by reading it in full. Tenant schema confirmed to have exactly slug/display_name/status/idp_realm_id (grep of tenant.ex field/1 calls) -- OQ-1's 'no backing column' premise is factually correct, not asserted. Verdicts on the three flagged open questions and the route-decision, as instructed: (1) Route-vs-discriminator decision (§1) ACCEPTED -- four independently sufficient reasons given (allowlist isolation, moduledoc scope, no existing integration to preserve, project's one-module-per-concern convention), a real tradeoff analysis, not a placeholder. (2) OQ-1 (global, not per-tenant, config for locales/default_locale/branding/environment_kind) ACCEPTED as a legitimate scope boundary, not silent under-delivery -- it satisfies MOB-2's exact 5-field shape; the four fields have no per-tenant backing anywhere in the system today (also cited: REQ-127/MOB-7 finding that the web platform itself has no locale policy), so per-tenant values would require an out-of-scope migration this task explicitly did not authorize. (3) OQ-2 (no ?host= branch) ACCEPTED -- verified against docs/mobile/requirements.md MOB-2 text directly: 'resolve tenant identity from a deep-link subdomain or manual slug entry' happens client-side before the endpoint is called, and Letflow has zero host->tenant binding infrastructure today (confirmed in tenant_config.ex's own moduledoc), so a ?host= param would be dead weight, not a missing capability. (4) OQ-3 (branding sub-schema is the design's own proposal) ACCEPTED -- confirmed docs/mobile/requirements.md specifies no branding sub-schema anywhere, so a placeholder proposal flagged as revisable is the correct move, not a guess presented as fact. §9's exact-shape test strategy (Map.keys sorted-equality assertion, explicit expected key list) and §4/§6's unknown-slug anti-enumeration justification (exhaustive branch table, all byte-identical) are both concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV to build against without further judgement calls. Checklist: (a) every requirement acceptance criterion has a design element via §9's resolution-map table, no TBD/deferral language found (grepped for TBD/'to be determined'/'to be decided' -- only forward references to future out-of-scope requirements, not deferred current-scope work); (b) function signatures fully specified in §3 (handle_mobile_tenant_config/1, resolve_realm_id/1, mobile_config_map/1 with its exact concrete 5-key shape spelled out field-by-field, safe_get_tenant_by_slug/1, idp_base_url/0, environment_kind/0); (c) error handling stated as explicit tagged tuples ({:ok, %Tenant{}} | {:error, :not_found | :lookup_failed}) plus the never-error/fallthrough rule stated as explicit branches, nothing implicit; (d) cross-module dependencies listed in full in §10; (e) no .ex implementation code bodies present -- §3 is @spec/comment only, and the two single-line snippets present (the Router forward/2 declaration in §2, and the terminal match _ do Response.not_found(conn) end in §3) are declarative routing lines with no business logic, matching the exact pattern already accepted in the precedent design lib/letflow/design/req078-supporting-routes.md (grepped: same forward(...) and match _ do Response.not_found(conn) end lines appear there too), not a new precedent being set by this validator. One MINOR non-blocking note recorded under issues: §3's mobile_config_map/1 @spec writes the map-key type as required(String) instead of the correct Dialyzer syntax required(String.t()) -- does not block ELIXIR-DEV since the concrete field-by-field shape immediately below it is unambiguous, but should be corrected when the real @spec is written.
